scope: Three missing IWO officers held in political immigration proceedings; preserve bail-separated periods and incomplete date precision.

guardian1950.label: National Guardian, July 26, 1950, p.4, Elmer Bendiner, Full-scale attack opens on foreign-born in U.S.; identifies Andrew Dmytryshyn, his IWO section leadership and photograph.

october.label: Naujienos, October 27, 1952, p.1, 8 komunistai Ellis Islande; names the eight detainees and reports their transfer after bail revocation. Original scan reviewed.

jldec.label: Jewish Life, December 1952, p.10, Ellis Island as Concentration Camp; names eight detained people but supplies November 17, conflicting with the October report.

jljan.label: Theodore Jacobs, Jewish Life, January 1953, p.16, Will the Racist Law Remain?; Dmytryshin November parole and Milgrom guarded hospitalization.

zecker.label: Robert M. Zecker, A Road to Peace and Freedom (Temple University Press, 2018), p.241 and notes 85-87; Milgrom hospitalization and eventual freedom. Litigation length is not continuous jail time.

iwoarchive.label: Cornell Kheel Center, International Workers Order records, collection 5276; leadership records include Sam Milgram spelling.

mezeicourt.label: Shaughnessy v. United States ex rel. Mezei, 345 U.S.206 (1953), pp.208-209; arrival, exclusion, failed removals, long Ellis Island detention and intervening bond release.

mezeiresearch.label: Charles D. Weisselberg, The Exclusion and Detention of Aliens, 143 University of Pennsylvania Law Review 933 (1995), pp.971 note 203, 974, 976, 982-983; archival reconstruction of IWO role and separate custody periods.

mezeilater.label: Julie Chinitz, Shiftiness: The Border in Eight Cases, ZYZZYVA, March 16, 2017; recounts Mezei parole and return to Buffalo in 1954.

prisoner.name: Andrew Dmytryshyn
prisoner.description: Andrew Dmytryshyn was a leader of the Ukrainian American Fraternal Union, a section of the International Workers Order. His political associations became the subject of deportation proceedings, and he was held at Ellis Island after his bail was revoked.

cases.charges: Civil immigration detention pending political deportation proceedings
cases.sentence: Held at Ellis Island in 1952 after bail revocation. Contemporary reports disagree on the recommitment date; only the year is entered. A later report confirms parole in November 1952. No criminal prison sentence or six-month term actually served is asserted.

case_research.custody_evidence: The October 27 newspaper names him among the eight transferred detainees; the later report records November parole, establishing custody beyond the initial arrest period.

entries.custody_evidence: The October 27 newspaper names him among the eight transferred detainees; the later report records November parole, establishing custody beyond the initial arrest period.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. Earlier 1950 arrest and bail are documented, but the duration of that separate detention is unresolved. November 17 in Jewish Life conflicts with the October 27 account. The six-month legal limit mentioned in the parole report is not proof of his actual time served. Reported age 58 does not establish an exact birthday. Genealogical dates have not been linked securely to this organizer.

photo.identity_evidence: Single portrait captioned ANDREW DMYTRYSHYN below the photograph in the July26,1950 National Guardian p.4 article about this IWO officer.

prisoner.name: Sam Milgrom
prisoner.description: Sam Milgrom was the national executive secretary of the International Workers Order. During the campaign to deport immigrant political organizers, he was confined at Ellis Island and later held under guard in a hospital.

cases.charges: Civil immigration detention pending political deportation proceedings
cases.sentence: Recommitted after bail cancellation in 1952. He remained detained for weeks and was moved to hospital under guard because of serious illness. Hospital transfer did not end his custody. Subsequent historical research confirms that he eventually gained freedom; the exact release date remains unverified.

case_research.custody_evidence: Contemporary autumn and December accounts identify actual confinement and continuing guarded hospitalization, establishing multi-day custody.

entries.custody_evidence: Contemporary autumn and December accounts identify actual confinement and continuing guarded hospitalization, establishing multi-day custody.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. The case beginning with his 1950 arrest involved intervening bail; nearly three years of litigation is not a continuous three-year imprisonment. Only the verified 1952 recommitment is entered. Later freedom supports released=true without inventing an endpoint. Do not confuse this IWO officer with the gallerist born in 1952, or attach that namesake’s photograph, birthday or website. No vital dates verified.

prisoner.name: Ignatz Mezei
prisoner.description: Ignatz Mezei was a Buffalo carpenter and officer of the International Workers Order’s Hungarian lodge. After returning from Europe, he was detained at Ellis Island as an alleged security risk. His challenge to exclusion and confinement reached the United States Supreme Court.

cases.charges: Civil immigration exclusion on alleged security grounds; initial Ellis Island detention
cases.sentence: Arrived February 9, 1950 and was detained pending exclusion. Failed attempts to send him abroad interrupted his physical presence on Ellis Island, so no exact continuous-day total is asserted. He was released on bond May 10, 1952. This detention is separated from his later return to custody.

cases.charges: Civil immigration exclusion on alleged security grounds; return after Supreme Court decision
cases.sentence: Returned to Ellis Island April 22, 1953 after the Supreme Court reversed the bond ruling. Released on immigration parole in August 1954 and returned to Buffalo. The intervening period at home on bond is excluded; no criminal sentence is assigned.

case_research.custody_evidence: The Supreme Court opinion documents prolonged confinement and eventual bond release; the archival reconstruction supplies the actual1952 release date.
Archival research documents the1953 recommitment and1954 parole following more than a year of renewed confinement.

entries.custody_evidence: The Supreme Court opinion documents prolonged confinement and eventual bond release; the archival reconstruction supplies the actual1952 release date. Archival research documents the1953 recommitment and1954 parole following more than a year of renewed confinement.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. No conviction for espionage or other security offense is inferred from administrative exclusion. His IWO office is documented in the archival reconstruction; membership alone is not used as proof of a crime. The unrelated 1935 petty-larceny fine and disputed 1927 arrest are excluded. Failed removal voyages are not counted as an exact uninterrupted US-soil custody interval. Exact final release day, birth and death dates remain withheld.
